t: Section 3692(c) is amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”.

fable.w: On its face this section only swaps one date for another in an existing provision; it names no outside party, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The tempting reading is that section 3692 may be the veterans' education advisory committee provision in title 38, so the date change extends an advisory body with non-federal members. But the text does not identify the title or describe any consultation process, so that reading rests on an assumption outside the section.
fable.s: Section 3692(c) is amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”.

opus.w: Section 3692 is most likely 38 U.S.C. 3692, which sets up the Veterans' Advisory Committee on Education, and subsection (c) sets the committee's end date. The committee includes non-federal members, such as veterans and education representatives, who advise the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, so extending it continues outside participation in federal decisions. The tempting 'No' reading treats this as a bare date change, but the date being changed is how long an advisory body with outside members stays in existence.
opus.s: Section 3692(c) is amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** On its face this is just a technical date change. It says nothing about consultation, hearings, or outside parties, so it would be easy to label it "No."

2. **Why I lean "Yes":** Using ordinary legal background knowledge, the "Section 3692" amended here is most likely 38 U.S.C. § 3692. That section sets up the Veterans' Advisory Committee on Education, and subsection (c) sets the date the committee ends. The committee advises the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and includes people from outside the federal government, such as veterans and education representatives. Extending its life by a year keeps that outside advisory input going into federal decisions. This is uncertain because the section never names the committee, and a reader working only from the text would see no participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple technical amendment that changes a specific date in another statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with non-federal entities. There is no interaction with parties outside the federal government described in this text.
qwen_chat.s: Section 3692(c) is amended by striking “December 31, 2013” and inserting “December 31, 2014”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a date could affect future participation processes, but the text itself contains no procedural requirements for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a technical amendment to a deadline.
